title: Measure Preserving Transformations and Poincare Recurrence

items.title: No-return sets have disjoint null preimage towers
items.statement: Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu,T)$ be a measure-preserving system with $\mu(X)<\infty$. For $E\in\mathcal A$ put $W=E\setminus\bigcup_{n\ge1}T^{-n}E$. Then the measurable sets $T^{-n}W$, $n\ge0$, are pairwise disjoint and all have measure zero.
items.strategy: Authored argument and exact inputs are in items/lem-no-return-sets-have-null-preimage-towers.md and the batch proof contract. If x belongs to preimages at i<j, T^i x∈W returns to E at time j-i, contradiction. N equal masses are bounded by μ(X).

items.title: Poincare recurrence for finite measure-preserving systems
items.statement: In a measure-preserving system $(X,\mathcal A,\mu,T)$ with $\mu(X)<\infty$, for every $E\in\mathcal A$ almost every $x\in E$ has $T^nx\in E$ for infinitely many positive integers $n$.
items.strategy: Authored argument and exact inputs are in items/thm-poincare-recurrence-for-finite-measure-preserving-systems.md and the batch proof contract. Every finite-return point eventually enters W at its last visit; hence the exceptional set is contained in union_{n≥0}T^-n W. This also includes points with no positive return.

items.title: Topological recurrence on second-countable spaces
items.statement: Let $X$ have a countable open basis contained in $\mathcal A$, and let $T$ preserve a finite measure $\mu$ on $(X,\mathcal A)$. Outside one measurable null set, every neighborhood of $x$ is revisited infinitely often by its positive orbit. If the topology is induced by a metric $d$, there are strictly increasing positive integers $n_j$ with $T^{n_j}x\to x$.
items.strategy: Authored argument and exact inputs are in items/cor-topological-poincare-recurrence-on-second-countable-spaces.md and the batch proof contract. Apply recurrence separately to every basis set, take the countable union of exceptional sets, and then choose the least succeeding time into a shrinking ball.

items.title: First-return times and induced transformations
items.statement:
Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu,T)$ preserve finite measure and let $E\in\mathcal A$ satisfy $\mu(E)>0$. For $x\in E$ define the **first-return time**

$$r_E(x)=\min\{n\ge1:T^nx\in E\},\qquad\min\varnothing=\infty.$$

A nonempty set of return times has a least element by [[thm-well-ordering-principle]]. Define the **infinitely returning core**

$$E_\infty=E\cap\bigcap_{N\ge1}\bigcup_{n\ge N}T^{-n}E.$$

This is the set-limsup convention of [[def-set-limsup-and-liminf]]. It is measurable by [[thm-sigma-algebra-closure-laws]], and [[thm-poincare-recurrence-for-finite-measure-preserving-systems]] gives $\mu(E\setminus E_\infty)=0$. Define the **induced transformation** and normalized measure by

$$T_E:E_\infty\longrightarrow E_\infty,\qquad T_E(x)=T^{r_E(x)}x,\qquad \mu_E(B)=\frac{\mu(B)}{\mu(E)},\quad B\in\mathcal A|_{E_\infty}.$$

Here the trace is as in [[def-trace-sigma-algebra]]. Since $E_\infty$ is measurable, the trace equals $\{B\in\mathcal A:B\subseteq E_\infty\}$: each intersection with $E_\infty$ is measurable and each such $B$ equals $B\cap E_\infty$. Its closure under relative complement and countable union follows directly from these same operations in $\mathcal A$; no sequence of ambient representatives needs to be chosen. This supplies the measurable-subset instance of [[thm-trace-is-a-sigma-algebra]] locally.

For $x\in E_\infty$, $r_E(x)$ is finite, and the infinitely many visits after $r_E(x)$ are exactly positive visits of $T_E(x)$, so $T_E(x)\in E_\infty$. Restricting countable additivity of $\mu$ and dividing by the positive finite number $\mu(E)$ makes $\mu_E$ a measure; its total mass is $\mu(E_\infty)/\mu(E)=1$. The value $\infty$ is allowed for $r_E$ on $E\setminus E_\infty$, but is never used as an iterate in $T_E$. No choice axiom enters this construction.
items.strategy: Authored argument and exact inputs are in items/def-first-return-time-and-induced-transformation.md and the batch proof contract. Use the infinitely-returning core, not merely the first-return domain: recurrence makes it conull in E and it is mapped into itself. Every trace-measurable B⊆E∞ equals A∩E∞ for some A∈A and hence belongs to A, so μ_E is well defined; μ(E∞)=μ(E) makes it a probability.

items.title: First-return time and induced map are measurable
items.statement: With $E,r_E,E_\infty,T_E$ as in the first-return definition, $r_E:E\to\{1,2,\ldots\}\cup\{\infty\}$ is measurable for the full power-set sigma-algebra on this countable target, and $T_E$ is measurable for $\mathcal A|_{E_\infty}$.
items.strategy: Authored argument and exact inputs are in items/prop-first-return-time-and-induced-map-are-measurable.md and the batch proof contract. The level r_E=n is E∩T^-n E∩intersection_{1≤j<n}T^-j(E^c). On each level T_E=T^n; take countable unions of preimages.

items.title: Induced transformations preserve restricted finite measure
items.statement: For a finite measure-preserving system and a measurable $E$ with $\mu(E)>0$, its induced transformation $T_E$ on $E_\infty$ preserves both $\mu|_{E_\infty}$ and $\mu_E$. Neither invertibility nor ergodicity is required.
items.strategy: Authored argument and exact inputs are in items/thm-induced-transformation-preserves-the-restricted-measure.md and the batch proof contract. For B⊆E∞ expand μ(B) by pulling back and splitting at E for N steps. The sum of first-return contributions is ≤μ(B). Apply the same inequality to E∞\B and use T_E^-1 E∞=E∞ to obtain equality.

items.title: Inducing an ergodic system gives an ergodic system
items.statement: If $T$ is an ergodic probability-preserving transformation and $\mu(E)>0$, then $T_E$ on $E_\infty$ is ergodic for $\mu_E$.
items.strategy: Authored argument and exact inputs are in items/prop-inducing-preserves-ergodicity.md and the batch proof contract. Extend a bounded T_E-invariant function along first entrance into E∞; sweep-out makes this defined a.e.; the extension is T-invariant, hence constant.

items.title: Kac return-time formula without invertibility
items.statement: If $T$ preserves an ergodic probability measure and $E$ is measurable with $\mu(E)>0$, then $\int_Er_E\,d\mu=1$. Equivalently, $\int_{E_\infty}r_E\,d\mu_E=1/\mu(E)$. The formula does not require invertibility.
items.strategy: Authored argument and exact inputs are in items/thm-kac-return-time-formula.md and the batch proof contract. Let C_N=intersection_{j=0}^{N-1}T^-j(E^c). Pullback invariance gives μ(E∩{r_E>j})=μ(C_j)-μ(C_{j+1}), with C_0=X. Sum j<N, use sweep-out for μ(C_N)→0, then monotone convergence of tail sums.

items.title: Kac integral formula for excursions
items.statement: In an ergodic probability-preserving system, let $\mu(E)>0$. For nonnegative measurable $f:X\to[0,\infty]$, define $S_Ef(x)=\sum_{j=0}^{r_E(x)-1}f(T^jx)$ on E, using the infinite nonnegative sum when $r_E(x)=\infty$. Then $\int_E S_Ef\,d\mu=\int_Xf\,d\mu$. For integrable real or complex f the excursion is absolutely summable a.e. on E; setting it to zero on its measurable null failure set gives the same identity.
items.strategy: Authored argument and exact inputs are in items/thm-kac-integral-formula-for-excursions.md and the batch proof contract. Repeatedly split the integral into E and E^c after pullback. For bounded nonnegative f the remainder is ≤||f||∞ times the measure of avoiding E for N steps. Truncate and use monotone convergence; apply first to |f| before signed decomposition.

items.title: The circle, rotations and the doubling map
items.statement:
The **circle** is $\mathbb T=[0,1)$ with distance $d(x,y)=\min(|x-y|,1-|x-y|)=\min_{k\in\mathbb Z}|x-y-k|$. The minimum is attained, since $-1<x-y<1$. It is nonnegative and symmetric, and it vanishes precisely when $x=y$. For minimizing integers k,l, $d(x,z)\le|x-z-(k+l)|\le|x-y-k|+|y-z-l|=d(x,y)+d(y,z)$, proving the triangle inequality.

Write $\{u\}=u-\lfloor u\rfloor\in[0,1)$ for fractional part. The **rotation** of angle $\alpha\in\mathbb R$ and the **doubling map** are

$$R_\alpha(x)=\{x+\alpha\},\qquad D(x)=\{2x\}.$$

They satisfy $d(R_\alpha x,R_\alpha y)=d(x,y)$ and $d(Dx,Dy)\le2d(x,y)$ by the integer-minimum formula, so are continuous in the circle metric. This topology differs from the ordinary interval topology at zero: points tending to 1 from below tend to 0 on the circle.

Open circle balls of radius less than $1/2$ are single ordinary intervals or two intervals meeting the cut at 0 and 1. By [[lem-q-and-irrationals-dense-r]], [[thm-rationals-countable]] and [[thm-product-of-countable]], balls with rational centers and positive rational radii form a countable base: given a ball about x, take a rational center close enough to x and a smaller rational radius whose ball contains x and stays inside the original ball. Thus circle-open sets are countable unions of ordinary Borel sets. Conversely ordinary interval-open subsets of $(0,1)$ are circle-open, and the singleton $\{0\}$ is circle-closed. Every relatively open subset of $[0,1)$ is therefore circle-Borel. The two Borel sigma-algebras agree.

For measures we **assume countable choice** [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $\lambda$ be the restriction of [[def-lebesgue-measure-and-the-lebesgue-sigma-algebra]] to $[0,1)$, either on Borel sets or on Lebesgue measurable sets. The measure and volume clauses of [[thm-lebesgue-measure-is-a-complete-measure]] give its total mass one: singletons have measure zero by covering them with intervals of arbitrarily small length, so changing an interval endpoint does not change length. By [[cor-lebesgue-sigma-algebra-is-the-completion-of-borel-lebesgue-measure]], the latter version is the completion of the former (intersect its Borel representatives and null covers with $[0,1)$). Countable choice is used for these measure constructions only; the circle metric and maps above are choice-free.
items.strategy: Authored argument and exact inputs are in items/def-circle-rotation-and-doubling-map.md and the batch proof contract. Check the circle metric and countable arc base; distinguish it from the ordinary interval topology. Both maps are continuous in the circle metric.

items.title: Circle rotations preserve Lebesgue measure
items.statement: Assume countable choice. For every real $\alpha$, $R_\alpha$ is an invertible measure-preserving transformation for both Borel Lebesgue probability on the circle and its completion.
items.strategy: Authored argument and exact inputs are in items/prop-circle-rotations-preserve-lebesgue-measure.md and the batch proof contract. Split a wrapping interval at the endpoint, use translation invariance and the finite pi-system criterion, then completion.

items.title: Irrational circle orbits are dense
items.statement: For irrational $\alpha$, the subgroup $\{\{n\alpha\}:n\in\mathbb Z\}$ is dense in the circle. For every $\varepsilon>0$ and integer $M\ge0$ there is an integer $n>M$ with $d(\{n\alpha\},0)<\varepsilon$. These assertions are choice-free.
items.strategy: Authored argument and exact inputs are in items/lem-irrational-circle-orbits-are-dense.md and the batch proof contract. Pigeonhole two of 0,α,...,Nα into the same one of N arcs. The nonzero difference is arbitrarily close to an integer; multiples give a fine net. Unboundedness follows because no fixed nonzero multiple is an integer.

references.title: E–W Proposition 2.16 p.26 and Example 2.33 p.49

items.title: Circle rotation is ergodic for Lebesgue measure exactly at irrational angles
items.statement: Assume countable choice. The circle rotation $R_\alpha$ is ergodic for Borel Lebesgue probability and for its completion if and only if $\alpha$ is irrational.
items.strategy: Authored argument and exact inputs are in items/thm-circle-rotation-is-ergodic-iff-angle-is-irrational.md and the batch proof contract. Rational case: finite union of short translates. Irrational case: take density points of an invariant set and its complement; choose a common small radius with both density ratios >0.9, and rotate the first center within radius/10 of the second using orbit density. The translated almost-full interval must overlap the other almost-full interval in positive measure, contradiction.

items.title: Integer-base maps and b-adic circle intervals
items.statement:
On the circle of [[def-circle-rotation-and-doubling-map]], for an integer $b\ge2$ put $D_b(x)=\{bx\}$. For every $n\ge0$ its **level-n b-adic intervals** are

$$I_{n,k}=[k/b^n,(k+1)/b^n),\qquad 0\le k<b^n.$$

These intervals partition $[0,1)$; at level zero the only interval is the whole circle. On the branch $I_{1,j}$ the map is $D_b(x)=bx-j$. Iterating fractional-part arithmetic gives $D_b^n(x)=\{b^nx\}$, and on $I_{n,k}$ this is $b^nx-k$. Each branch maps bijectively onto $[0,1)$ with inverse $y\mapsto(y+k)/b^n$. Half-open endpoints ensure that every x belongs to exactly one branch, including x=0. Multiplication by the integer b respects congruence modulo one, and the distance formula gives $d(D_bx,D_by)\le b\,d(x,y)$. Thus these are continuous circle maps. The previously defined doubling map is exactly $D=D_2$. None of these algebraic or metric facts uses a measure or a choice axiom.
items.strategy: Authored argument and exact inputs are in items/def-integer-base-map-on-the-circle.md and the batch proof contract. This is the circle endomorphism induced by multiplication by b. Record its b affine branches, the b-adic interval convention, and D=D_2 for later stable doubling specializations.

references.title: E–W Example 2.4 pp.14–15; MT-22 binding base-b amendment

items.title: Integer-base circle maps preserve Lebesgue measure
items.statement: Assume countable choice. For every integer $b\ge2$, the circle map $D_b$ is continuous, surjective and non-injective, and preserves Borel Lebesgue probability and its completion.
items.strategy: Authored argument and exact inputs are in items/prop-integer-base-map-preserves-lebesgue-measure.md and the batch proof contract. For a half-open interval [a,c), its inverse image is the disjoint union over 0≤j<b of [(a+j)/b,(c+j)/b), with total length c-a. Apply the finite-measure generating-pi-system criterion, then the completion clause. Continuity is in the circle metric; surjectivity and non-injectivity have explicit branch witnesses.

items.title: Every integer-base circle map is strongly mixing
items.statement: Assume countable choice. For every integer $b\ge2$ and every pair of Borel or completed Lebesgue measurable circle sets A,B, $\lambda(A\cap D_b^{-n}B)\to\lambda(A)\lambda(B)$. Thus $D_b$ is strongly mixing for either measure.
items.strategy: Authored argument and exact inputs are in items/thm-integer-base-map-is-strongly-mixing.md and the batch proof contract. For b-adic intervals I,J of depths r,s and n≥r, I∩D_b^-n J is a disjoint union of b^{n-r} intervals of length b^{-(n+s)}, hence has measure λ(I)λ(J). Apply the mixing generator criterion on the Borel sigma-algebra. Replacing completed sets by Borel cores modulo null sets transfers the correlation limit to the completion.

references.title: Sarig Proposition 1.5 p.9, b-adic branch-count generalization

items.title: Doubling preserves Lebesgue measure
items.statement: Assume countable choice. The doubling map $D(x)=\{2x\}$ is a continuous, surjective, non-injective transformation preserving Borel Lebesgue probability on the circle and its completion.
items.strategy: Authored argument and exact inputs are in items/prop-doubling-map-preserves-lebesgue-measure.md and the batch proof contract. Specialize the integer-base preservation proposition to b=2. Explicitly, the preimage of [a,c) is [a/2,c/2) disjoint union [(a+1)/2,(c+1)/2), while D(0)=D(1/2).

items.title: Doubling is ergodic for Lebesgue measure
items.statement: Assume countable choice. Doubling is ergodic for Borel Lebesgue probability and its completion.
items.strategy: Authored argument and exact inputs are in items/thm-doubling-map-is-ergodic-for-lebesgue-measure.md and the batch proof contract. For a strict invariant A and every generation-n dyadic interval I, branch D^n maps I linearly onto [0,1), giving λ(A∩I)=λ(A)λ(I). A density point of A has dyadic density tending to one: I is contained in a centered interval of twice its length. Hence λ(A)=1 if positive.

references.title: Sarig Proposition 1.5 p.9, conclusion; density argument is the MT-22 prescribed local replacement

items.title: Doubling is strongly mixing for Lebesgue measure
items.statement: Assume countable choice. Doubling is strongly mixing for Borel Lebesgue probability and for its completion: $\lambda(A\cap D^{-n}B)\to\lambda(A)\lambda(B)$ for every pair of measurable circle sets.
items.strategy: Authored argument and exact inputs are in items/prop-doubling-map-is-strongly-mixing.md and the batch proof contract. Specialize the integer-base strong-mixing theorem to b=2; its b-adic branch count is exactly the dyadic calculation.

items.title: Binary-sequence cylinders and fair-coin content
items.statement:
Put $\Omega=\{0,1\}^{\mathbb N_0}$, the set of functions from nonnegative integers to $\{0,1\}$. For a finite set $F\subseteq\mathbb N_0$ and a function $a:F\to\{0,1\}$ the **cylinder** $[a]_F$ consists of x with $x_j=a(j)$ for every j in F. The empty prescription gives all of Omega. Every cylinder is nonempty by filling unspecified coordinates with zero.

The **cylinder algebra** $\mathcal C$ is the set of finite unions of cylinders, including the empty union. It is an algebra in the sense of [[def-algebra-of-subsets]]: any finite list of prescriptions can be refined to their finite coordinate union G; the $2^{|G|}$ complete prescriptions on G are disjoint nonempty atoms partitioning Omega, and union, intersection and complement of unions of these atoms again are such unions.

Give each G-atom mass $2^{-|G|}$. If A is a union of m distinct G-atoms, define its **fair-coin content** by $p_0(A)=m2^{-|G|}$. This is independent of G and its representation. Enlarging G to H splits each atom into exactly $2^{|H|-|G|}$ atoms, leaving its mass unchanged. Two representations agree after refining to their coordinate union; because all refined atoms are nonempty, the same subset A selects precisely the same atoms in both. Common refinement also proves finite additivity on disjoint sets. In particular $p_0(\varnothing)=0$, $p_0(\Omega)=1$, and $p_0([a]_F)=2^{-|F|}$. All constructions here involve finite coordinate sets and are choice-free.
items.strategy: Authored argument and exact inputs are in items/def-binary-sequence-cylinders-and-fair-coin-content.md and the batch proof contract. Use the algebra of finite unions of cylinders, not the collection of cylinders alone. Common refinement proves the content is well-defined and finitely additive.

items.title: Binary-sequence space is compact without Tychonoff
items.statement: On $\Omega=\{0,1\}^{\mathbb N_0}$ put $d(x,x)=0$ and $d(x,y)=2^{-\min\{j:x_j\ne y_j\}}$ for $x\ne y$. This is a metric whose topology is generated by cylinders; it is compact in ZF.
items.strategy: Authored argument and exact inputs are in items/lem-binary-sequence-space-is-compact-without-tychonoff.md and the batch proof contract. If an open cover has no finite subcover, choose recursively the first binary child cylinder still having no finite subcover. The resulting unique path belongs to a covering open set which contains one of its prefix cylinders, contradiction. No arbitrary choice.

references.title: E–W Examples 2.8–2.9 compact metric footnote; elementary binary-tree proof

items.title: Fair-coin cylinder content is a premeasure
items.statement: The fair-coin content $p_0$ on the cylinder algebra $\mathcal C$ is a finite premeasure, with $p_0(\Omega)=1$. This assertion is choice-free.
items.strategy: Authored argument and exact inputs are in items/lem-fair-coin-cylinder-content-is-a-premeasure.md and the batch proof contract. A countable disjoint union in the algebra covering an algebra member is an open cover of a compact clopen set. A finite subcover reduces countable additivity to finite additivity; remaining members are empty.

items.title: Fair-coin measure on binary sequences
items.statement: Assume countable choice. There is a unique Borel probability $p$ on binary sequence space such that a cylinder prescribing k distinct coordinates has mass $2^{-k}$. Its completion is a complete probability measure on the completion of the Borel sigma-algebra.
items.strategy: Authored argument and exact inputs are in items/thm-fair-coin-measure-on-binary-sequences.md and the batch proof contract. Apply Caratheodory to the premeasure; prefix cylinders are a countable base, so the generated sigma-algebra is Borel. This is not a general infinite-product theorem.

references.title: E–W Examples 2.8–2.9 with local Caratheodory route

items.title: The fair-coin one-sided shift preserves measure and is mixing
items.statement: Assume countable choice. The one-sided left shift $\sigma:\Omega\to\Omega$, $(\sigma x)_j=x_{j+1}$, preserves the fair-coin probability and its completion, is strongly mixing for both, and hence is ergodic.
items.strategy: Authored argument and exact inputs are in items/thm-fair-coin-one-sided-shift-is-measure-preserving-and-mixing.md and the batch proof contract. Preimages preserve cylinder masses; widely separated coordinate sets give exactly independent cylinders by finite counting. Apply the generator criteria on the Borel sigma-algebra, transfer preservation and correlations to completed sets modulo null sets, and use the mixing implication.

items.title: A countable dense family of continuous functions on a compact metric space
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. If $(K,d)$ is a nonempty compact metric space, there is a sequence $(f_j)_{j\ge1}$ in $C(K,\mathbb R)$ such that for every $f\in C(K,\mathbb R)$ and $\varepsilon>0$ some $j$ satisfies $\|f-f_j\|_\infty<\varepsilon$. One may use all rational polynomials in finitely many distance functions to an enumerated dense subset, including the rational constant functions.
items.strategy: The authored proof uses all-witness finite covers and lattice maxima/minima to prove uniform density, then rational coefficients and explicit countability to obtain a countable family. AC_omega covers the inherited lattice approximation use; no choice indexed by K is made.

references.title: E–W §4.1 pp.97–98, replacing weak-star compactness with the design-required local argument

items.title: A compact-metric probability representation using countable choice
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ be a nonempty compact metric space and let $\Lambda:C(K,\mathbb R)\to\mathbb R$ be real-linear, positive in the sense that $f\ge0$ implies $\Lambda(f)\ge0$, and normalized by $\Lambda(1)=1$. Then there is a Borel probability $\mu$ on $K$ with $\Lambda(f)=\int_K f\,d\mu$ for every continuous real $f$. It is outer regular on Borel sets and inner regular on open sets by compact subsets. No Dependent Choice is required.
items.strategy: Authored argument and exact inputs are in items/lem-positive-functionals-on-compact-metric-spaces-have-probability-representations.md and the batch proof contract. Explicit metric cutoffs and finite partitions yield an outer measure; prove open-set splitting, compact formula and slice approximation locally, avoiding the DC-based general LCH construction.

references.title: Compact-metric adaptation of the RMK construction; Cohn, Measure Theory, 2nd ed., Chapter 7

items.title: Probability sequences on compact metric spaces have integral-convergent subsequences
items.statement: Assume countable choice. Let $(\mu_n)_{n\ge1}$ be Borel probabilities on a nonempty compact metric space $K$. There are strictly increasing positive integers $n_r$ and a Borel probability $\mu$ on $K$ such that $\int f\,d\mu_{n_r}\to\int f\,d\mu$ for every $f\in C(K,\mathbb R)$. The limiting probability can be taken outer regular on Borel sets and inner regular on open sets.
items.strategy: The authored proof uses deterministic nested bisection and least surviving indices for the countable dense test family, extends the limit functional uniformly, and applies the fully authored compact-metric representation lemma under AC_omega.

references.title: E–W §4.1 pp.97–98; local diagonal/RMK replacement for source weak-star compactness

items.title: Krylov–Bogolyubov existence of an invariant probability
items.statement: Assume countable choice. Every continuous self-map $T:K\to K$ of a nonempty compact metric space admits a Borel probability $\mu$ satisfying $\mu(T^{-1}E)=\mu(E)$ for every Borel $E\subseteq K$. Thus $(K,\mathcal B(K),\mu,T)$ is a measure-preserving probability system.
items.strategy: Authored argument and exact inputs are in items/thm-krylov-bogolyubov-for-nonempty-compact-metric-spaces.md and the batch proof contract. Average point masses along one orbit and use the previous subsequence lemma. Telescoping bounds the discrepancy for f∘T and f by 2||f||∞/N. Define the pushforward by inverse images; prove its integration identity first for indicators, then finite simple functions, and then directly from the supremum definition of the nonnegative integral before signed decomposition. It is Borel and regular, so RMK uniqueness gives equality. Do not invoke Banach–Alaoglu.

items.title: False: measure-preserving transformations are invertible
items.statement: The assertion that every measure-preserving probability transformation is invertible, even after restriction to an invariant conull set, is false. Assuming countable choice, doubling on the Lebesgue circle is a counterexample.
items.strategy: Authored argument and exact inputs are in items/fs-measure-preserving-transformations-are-invertible.md and the batch proof contract. D(0)=D(1/2), so actual invertibility fails. If D were injective on a conull C with null complement N, then for each x∈[0,1/2) at least one of x,x+1/2 lies in N. Thus [0,1/2)⊆N∪(N-1/2), a null set by translation invariance and finite subadditivity, contradiction.

items.title: False: ergodicity implies strong mixing
items.statement: Assuming countable choice, the assertion that every ergodic probability-preserving transformation is strongly mixing is false: any irrational circle rotation gives a counterexample.
items.strategy: Authored argument and exact inputs are in items/fs-ergodicity-implies-strong-mixing.md and the batch proof contract. Return subsequence n_j α→0 gives correlation of a half-circle with itself tending to 1/2 instead of 1/4.

items.title: False: Poincare recurrence needs no finite total measure
items.statement: Poincaré recurrence is false if the finite-total-measure hypothesis is omitted. Assuming countable choice, $T(x)=x+1$ on $(\mathbb R,\mathcal L,\lambda)$ preserves measure, but no point of the positive-measure set $E=[0,1)$ ever returns to $E$ at a positive time.
items.strategy: Authored argument and exact inputs are in items/fs-poincare-recurrence-without-finite-total-measure.md and the batch proof contract. Preimages translate sets, whereas positive iterates of [0,1) are disjoint from it.

items.title: False: an ergodic invariant sigma-algebra has only two sets
items.statement: Assuming countable choice, it is false that an ergodic system has only the empty set and the whole space as strictly invariant measurable sets. For Lebesgue doubling on $[0,1)$, the dyadic rationals form a nonempty proper strictly invariant null set.
items.strategy: Authored argument and exact inputs are in items/fs-ergodicity-forces-only-empty-and-full-invariant-sets.md and the batch proof contract. For doubling the dyadic rationals in [0,1) form a nonempty proper null set with D^-1 Q_2=Q_2.

items.title: False: every orbit of an ergodic system is dense
items.statement: Assuming countable choice, an ergodic probability-preserving continuous map need not have every orbit dense. Lebesgue doubling on the circle is ergodic, but the forward orbit of zero is the singleton $\{0\}$.
items.strategy: Authored argument and exact inputs are in items/fs-ergodicity-forces-every-orbit-dense.md and the batch proof contract. Zero is fixed and the circle has other points.

items.title: False: constant continuous invariants characterize measure ergodicity
items.statement: The assertion that a probability-preserving continuous map is measure ergodic whenever all of its everywhere invariant continuous real functions are constant is false. On the circle, doubling has only constant everywhere invariant continuous functions, but is not ergodic for $\mu=\tfrac12\delta_0+\tfrac14\delta_{1/3}+\tfrac14\delta_{2/3}$. This atomic counterexample is choice-free, and therefore also holds under countable choice.
items.strategy: Authored argument and exact inputs are in items/fs-continuous-invariant-functions-characterize-measure-ergodicity.md and the batch proof contract. For D, f∘D=f and the density of preimages of zero force every continuous invariant f constant. Use μ=(δ_0+(δ_{1/3}+δ_{2/3})/2)/2; the invariant set of eventual preimages of 0 has μ=1/2.

references.title: E–W ergodicity definition and doubling example; explicit measure specialization

title: Measure Preserving Transformations and Poincare Recurrence — Examples

items.title: An explicit invariant set for a rational rotation
items.statement: Assume countable choice. If $\alpha=p/q$ with integers $p$, $q\ge1$ in lowest terms, then $E=\bigcup_{j=0}^{q-1}[j/q,j/q+1/(2q))$ is strictly invariant under $R_\alpha$ and has Lebesgue measure $1/2$. Thus this rational rotation is not ergodic.
items.strategy: Authored argument and exact inputs are in items/ex-rational-rotation-invariant-set.md and the batch proof contract. Rotation permutes these intervals.

items.title: Dyadic preimages under doubling
items.statement: Assume countable choice. For doubling $D(x)=\{2x\}$ on the circle, $D^{-1}[0,1/2)=[0,1/4)\cup[1/2,3/4)$, of measure $1/2$. In contrast, $D[0,1/2)=[0,1)$ has measure one.
items.strategy: Authored argument and exact inputs are in items/ex-doubling-dyadic-preimage-computation.md and the batch proof contract. Compute both branches. Forward image D[0,1/2)=[0,1) has twice the measure.

items.title: Base-three cylinders and their preimages
items.statement: Assume countable choice. For $D_3(x)=\{3x\}$, one has $D_3^{-1}[0,1/3)=[0,1/9)\cup[1/3,4/9)\cup[2/3,7/9)$, of measure $1/3$. With $I_{n,k}=[k/3^n,(k+1)/3^n)$, $D_3(I_{2,3a+c})=I_{1,c}$ for $a,c\in\{0,1,2\}$: applying $D_3$ deletes the first ternary digit.
items.strategy: Authored argument and exact inputs are in items/ex-base-three-cylinder-intervals-and-preimages.md and the batch proof contract. Compute the three affine inverse branches and their lengths. For I_{2,3a+c}, 0≤a,c<3, calculate D_3(I_{2,3a+c})=I_{1,c}; half-open intervals remove endpoint ambiguity.

references.title: E–W Example 2.4 pp.14–15, base-three specialization; MT-22 binding example amendment

items.title: Fair-coin cylinder masses and separated blocks
items.statement: Assume countable choice. Index binary sequences by $0,1,2,\ldots$, and let $[a_0\cdots a_{r-1}]$ prescribe the first $r$ coordinates. For fair-coin probability $p$, $p([0])=1/2$, $p([01])=1/4$, $p([101])=1/8$, and $p([01]\cap\sigma^{-3}[10])=1/16$.
items.strategy: Authored argument and exact inputs are in items/ex-fair-coin-cylinder-measures-tabulated.md and the batch proof contract. Count distinct prescribed coordinates; no probabilistic independence theorem is assumed.

items.title: Recurrence to a dyadic interval under doubling
items.statement: Assume countable choice. For Lebesgue doubling and $E=[0,1/4)$, almost every $x\in E$ has $D^n x\in E$ for infinitely many positive integers $n$. The points of $E$ returning at time one form $[0,1/8)$, of measure $1/8$.
items.strategy: Authored argument and exact inputs are in items/ex-doubling-recurrence-to-a-dyadic-interval.md and the batch proof contract. Apply recurrence on the unit-probability circle. No every-point conclusion or return frequency is asserted.

items.title: Kac mean return to a half-circle under irrational rotation
items.statement: Assume countable choice. Let $\alpha$ be irrational, let $R_\alpha$ act on the Lebesgue circle, and put $E=[0,1/2]$. Its first positive return time satisfies $\int_E r_E\,d\lambda=1$. On the recurrent core $E_\infty$ with normalized restricted probability $\lambda_E$, the mean return time is $\int_{E_\infty}r_E\,d\lambda_E=2$.
items.strategy: Authored argument and exact inputs are in items/ex-kac-mean-return-to-a-half-circle.md and the batch proof contract. Apply Kac with λ(E)=1/2. Endpoints change no integral; no assertion that each return time equals two.

items.title: Mod-null invariance need not be strict invariance
items.statement: The assertion that every invariant-modulo-null-sets measurable set is strictly invariant is false. Assuming countable choice, for Lebesgue doubling the set $E=\{0\}$ satisfies $\lambda(D^{-1}E\mathbin\triangle E)=0$, but $D^{-1}E\ne E$.
items.strategy: Authored argument and exact inputs are in items/cex-mod-null-invariance-is-not-strict-invariance.md and the batch proof contract. Both finite sets are null; calculate the preimage.

items.title: Doubling ergodicity depends on the invariant measure
items.statement: The assertion that doubling has the same ergodicity behavior for every invariant probability is false. Assuming countable choice, it is ergodic for Lebesgue probability $\lambda$ and for $\delta_0$, but not for $\mu=\tfrac12\delta_0+\tfrac14\delta_{1/3}+\tfrac14\delta_{2/3}$.
items.strategy: Authored argument and exact inputs are in items/cex-doubling-ergodicity-depends-on-the-invariant-measure.md and the batch proof contract. The two periodic-orbit probabilities are invariant; their mixture assigns mass 1/2 to the strict invariant eventual-zero set. This corrects the design’s false δ_0 counterexample.

references.title: E–W Definition 2.13 and periodic orbit specialization

items.title: Irrational rotation is ergodic but not weakly mixing
items.statement: Assume countable choice. An irrational rotation $R_\alpha$ of the Lebesgue circle is ergodic but not weakly mixing. The single function $f(x)=e^{2\pi i x}$ has mean zero, and its centered absolute self-correlation equals one at every nonnegative iterate.
items.strategy: Authored argument and exact inputs are in items/cex-irrational-rotation-is-not-weakly-mixing.md and the batch proof contract. Use f(x)=exp(2πix), whose mean is zero and whose absolute self-correlation at every iterate is one. This is one explicit function computation, not the Fourier-series ergodicity proof.

items.title: Kac normalization needs ergodicity
items.statement: Assume countable choice. Removing ergodicity from Kac’s probability normalization is invalid. For the identity $T$ on $([0,1],\mathcal B([0,1]),\lambda)$ and $E=[0,1/2]$, every point of $E$ has $r_E=1$, but $\int_Er_E\,d\lambda=1/2$, not one. The normalized return mean is one, not $1/\lambda(E)=2$.
items.strategy: Authored argument and exact inputs are in items/cex-kac-formula-needs-ergodicity.md and the batch proof contract. Compute directly; normalized mean is one, not 1/λ(E).

items.title: The Gauss map preserves Gauss measure
items.statement: Assume countable choice. On $X=[0,1)$ put $G(0)=0$ and $G(x)=\{1/x\}$ for $x>0$. The Borel probability $\mu$ with density $h(x)=1/[\log(2)(1+x)]$ relative to Lebesgue measure is $G$-invariant. The same map preserves its completion. This example proves measure preservation only.
items.strategy: The authored proof normalizes by logarithmic interval integrals, computes exact inverse images of initial intervals, telescopes finite logarithmic sums, and applies finite-measure pi-system uniqueness and completion. A separate inverse-branch density sum is computed explicitly.
